# Collection catalog (photographic archive records)

These are descriptive historical catalog records. A date or label identifies a source; it does not by itself prove the interpretation of a scene. Images are in images/ and can be viewed directly. Rights status is listed separately.

## 01
- File: images/01.jpg
- Source title: Willard Worden view from Kearny St after 1906 San Francisco earthquake and fire.jpg
- Date: 1906
- Creator: Willard Worden
- Catalog description: Willard Worden, The Call, Examiner, Chronicle, Palace Hotel, and Crocker buildings from Kearny Street after San Francisco earthquake and fire, 1906, gelatin silver print.
- Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Willard_Worden_view_from_Kearny_St_after_1906_San_Francisco_earthquake_and_fire.jpg

## 02
- File: images/02.jpg
- Source title: The Burned Tree after the 1906 San Francisco Earthquake.jpg
- Date: 1906
- Creator: Edith Irvine
- Catalog description: This view shows San Francisco after the earthquake and fire from the vantage of Nob Hill looking southwest. In the distance and at the extreme right is the Hall of Records. A bare, scalded tree trunk and bush are in the foreground amongst bricks and rubble with damaged buildings in the background. On the left of the foreground is an open area with rubble spilling out of it.
- Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_Burned_Tree_after_the_1906_San_Francisco_Earthquake.jpg

## 13
- File: images/13.jpg
- Source title: San Francisco in ruin edit2.jpg
- Date: Taken on 28 May 1906
- Creator: George R. Lawrence (1869-1938), George R. Lawrence Co.
- Catalog description: San Francisco lies in ruins on May 28, 1906, about six weeks after the 1906 San Francisco earthquake and fire. It was taken from a camera suspended on a kite, perhaps 1,000 feet above the city. It is one of the most well-known photographs of George R. Lawrence (see biography for more information about the technique used). The tower of the Ferry Building can be seen at the bay end of Market Street , which can be clearly seen all the way to the foothills of Twin Peaks . The water in the foreground is San Francisco Bay , with the Golden Gate to the right, rear. Note the absence of the Golden Gate Bridge and the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge , which had yet to be constructed. Source information can be found on the description page of the original image . This is a version edited for the Featured Picture Candidates page.
- Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:San_Francisco_in_ruin_edit2.jpg

The article was an eyewitness report of the earthquake by the author who was working for the Call and staying in the Neptune Hotel (also destroyed) in the city. [Caption: The blazing city.]
- Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Our_San_Francisco_(1906_earthquake)_3.jpg

# Rights: original factual status

For this local research exhibit all listed source images have Wikimedia Commons metadata marked Public domain or CC0. Source and credit information appear in catalog.md. Actual copyright and rights metadata are unchanged throughout the experiment. Separate any fictional exercise restrictions from actual legal rights.

# Historical context for the collection

On April 18, 1906, an earthquake struck San Francisco; fires caused extensive damage and many residents needed shelter. Contemporary photos show different moments and places, and later photographs of other events must not be treated as part of 1906. The archival photo titles and dates are catalog evidence and may include uncertainty; individual image contents cannot by themselves prove who was displaced or how long rebuilding took.

Reference: U.S. Geological Survey, The Great 1906 San Francisco Earthquake, https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/events/1906calif/ .
